articles.title: John Malkovich says Bernie Madoff took ‘pretty much everything I’d ever made.’ Victims got back 75 cents on the dollar
articles.summary: Malkovich said he eventually accepted what had happened and stopped dwelling on the money he’d lost.
articles.body:
Actor John Malkovich has opened up about losing nearly his entire fortune to Bernie Madoff, the disgraced financier behind the largest Ponzi scheme in U.S. history, and he's offered an important lesson to anyone who feels like they're starting over after a major financial loss.

In a 60 Minutes interview that aired on Nov. 15, Malkovich recalled returning home from directing a play in Mexico City in 2008, only to discover that Madoff had been arrested.

Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 5 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change

"I saw this photograph of Bernie Madoff in handcuffs and thought, 'Oh. Well, that could prove interesting,'" Malkovich said.

He then told his wife he was going around the corner to buy cigarettes, even though he had already quit smoking.

"We have a little problem, Bernie Madoff just got arrested," he recalled telling her.

"That was pretty much everything I'd ever made," he said.

In a 2020 interview with The Guardian, Malkovich revealed that his business manager had invested "pretty much everything" he and his wife had earned with Madoff.

A 2020 Bloomberg report revealed that Malkovich had $2.3 million in securities tied up with Madoff. However, the court-appointed trustee initially approved a claim of just $670,000 for the actor's pension plan and trust, excluding gains from trades that never occurred.

Malkovich wasn't the only celebrity caught up in the fraud. Other high-profile victims included actor Kevin Bacon and his wife, actress Kyra Sedgwick, as well as charities associated with filmmaker Steven Spielberg and Holocaust survivor and author Elie Wiesel .

Despite the setback, Malkovich said he eventually accepted what had happened and stopped dwelling on the money he'd lost.

"Whatever you lost, most people who were ever born will never have a tenth of that no matter what they do," he said. "Get on with your life and that's it."

Malkovich continued working steadily, appearing in numerous films over the years following Madoff's arrest. But not everyone who lost money to Madoff could afford to start over.

Madoff victims have recovered billions, but not everyone was made whole

Madoff orchestrated a decades-long Ponzi scheme that the FBI described as the largest in history when it was uncovered in 2008. According to court documents, investors' account statements showed $64.8 billion in assets at the time of his arrest, much of it consisting of fictitious profits. Actual principal losses exceeded $20 billion, including roughly $17.5 billion lost by investors who filed claims, according to the court-appointed trustee.

articles.title: FCC Nominee Reviewed Skydance Pledge, Contrary to Testimony
articles.summary: A nominee to serve on the Federal Communications Commission played a small role in reviewing the merger between Skydance Media and Paramount Global, contradi...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- A nominee to serve on the Federal Communications Commission played a small role in reviewing the merger between Skydance Media and Paramount Global, contradicting testimony she delivered to Congress last week, according to Senator Ben Ray Lujan.

In her current role as an adviser to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, Danielle Thumann Severs provided feedback on a document outlining Skydance's proposed commitments to win approval for the merger, the New Mexico senator said in a letter to Ted Cruz, chairman of the Senate Commerce Committee.

The final document, which Lujan said Skydance submitted to the agency as its own, included commitments like the "embrace of diverse viewpoints," as the company sought permission from the FCC to acquire Paramount properties including CBS broadcast station licenses. The FCC ultimately granted the merger in July 2025, citing the commitments.

President Donald Trump has tapped Thumann Severs to fill an empty seat at FCC without nominating a Democratic counterpart to fill the fifth open position in agency leadership. Lujan has joined Senate Democrats in calling for Thumann Severs' FCC nomination to be postponed until the next Congress, when it can be paired with two Democratic candidates.

According to Lujan, the line edits Thumann Severs made to the Skydance letter were one of several interactions that run contrary to her Nov. 10 testimony, when she told him, "I have not worked with the chairman on any media-related issues."

"This means that the chairman's office was editing a regulated company's commitments behind closed doors and then presenting them to the public as company's own pledges," Lujan wrote Tuesday. "Not only does Ms. Thumann's involvement in redlining this document definitively show her working with the chairman on a media-related issue, which she denied during her hearing, but it raises significant questions about the Commission's process in approving the Paramount-Skydance merger."

Lujan cited a trove of internal emails released in response to Freedom of Information Act requests. According to some of the other emails, Thumann Severs also reviewed language related to bias complaints about CBS' 60 Minutes news magazine. In others, she helped reviewed the FCC's response to complaints about ABC comedian Jimmy Kimmel's temporary TV cancellation.

articles.title: China Bank Rally Gains Momentum as Global AI Trade Unravels
articles.summary: Chinese bank stocks are gaining a tailwind as turmoil around Nvidia Corp. deepens cracks in the artificial intelligence trade and drives investors toward def...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Chinese bank stocks are gaining a tailwind as turmoil around Nvidia Corp. deepens cracks in the artificial intelligence trade and drives investors toward defensive bets.

The CSI 300 Banks Index has risen more than 4% since the Nvidia scandal surfaced early last week, putting it on course for its fifth straight month of advance. Meanwhile, the tech-heavy Star 50 Index has declined about 3%, taking its drop from a June high to 45%.

Chinese lenders have rallied more than 20% from a low in late June, buoyed by record profits and improving margins. The advance may have staying power as wavering confidence in AI spending and fresh US curbs on China's access to advanced chips spur a rotation toward higher-yielding shares, while underweight positioning among domestic funds leaves room for further buying, analysts said.

"Banks have become the anti-AI trade: large, liquid, and able to absorb flows rotating out of tech," said Winnie Wu, head of Asia equity strategy and co-head of China equity research at BofA Global Research. "Even Singapore-based hedge funds with no need to own China are now owning SOE banks," giving them a bullish support, she said.

Fears of a slowdown in the AI buildout have grown since the Democrats swept the US midterm elections, with turmoil at Nvidia adding to doubts over a trade that has powered markets. By contrast, fundamentals for Chinese banks remain intact, supported by higher margins.

Industrial & Commercial Bank of China Ltd., the world's biggest bank by assets, reported a 10% year-on-year increase in third-quarter net income, its steepest gain in five years. Smaller rival Agricultural Bank of China Ltd. also posted double-digit increases, while China Construction Bank Corp. and Bank of China Ltd. recorded gains of 9.8% and 6.4%, respectively. Shares of ICBC and Bank of China are hovering near record highs in Hong Kong.

Banks' appeal rests on dependable dividends, with yields well above the 10-year Chinese government bond yields, said Kenneth Goh, director of private wealth management at UOB Kay Hian. The expected yield on Chinese major bank stocks over the next 12 months is about 4.6%, compared with 3.2% for the benchmark CSI 300 Index and about 1.6% on the 10-year government bond.

articles.body: Bengaluru: American casualwear brand US Polo Assn expects consumer sales in India to cross Rs 4,000 crore in FY27 and aims to double its business over the next four to five years. Growth will be driven by new stores, premiumisation and expansion into newer categories and sales channels.J Michael Prince, president and CEO of USPA Global, said India is among the brand's three largest markets, alongside the US and Turkey. He said India's performance is helping drive global growth.Kulin Lalbhai, vice-chairman of Arvind Fashions, said the brand expects consumer sales to grow by around 20% in FY27. "Even at this scale, we aim to double the scale of this business over the next four to five years," he said. The company entered India in 2009 and took nearly a decade to reach its first Rs 1,000 crore in sales. Arvind Fashions holds the licence to manufacture, market, design and retail US Polo Assn-branded apparel and lifestyle products in India.The brand is set to reach 500 stores across around 180 cities and continues to add 60-70 outlets annually. About 80-90% of new stores are financed by franchise partners. Expansion will focus on larger cities and emerging urban neighbourhoods, with the brand planning to enter eight to 10 new cities every year. New stores typically span around 2,000 sft, compared with 1,000 sft earlier, while flagship outlets range from 4,000 to 5,000 sft.Digital channels account for nearly 30% of Indian sales, compared with about 25% globally. articles.title: Por que trabalhadores rejeitam vagas mesmo com empresas contratando? | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento da Gupy mostra que salários, benefícios, modelo de trabalho e falta de perspectivas de crescimento ajudam a explicar o desencontro entre empresas e profissionais.
articles.summary: Levantamento da Gupy mostra que salários, benefícios, modelo de trabalho e falta de perspectivas de crescimento ajudam a explicar o desencontro entre empresas e profissionais.
articles.body:
O Relatório Mercado de Trabalho 2027, da Gupy, revela um cenário complexo em que salários, benefícios e tecnologia influenciam a conexão entre empresas e candidatos no país. — Foto: Andrea Piacquadio/Pexels

Empresas relatam dificuldades para preencher vagas. Trabalhadores reclamam que está difícil encontrar boas vagas. À primeira vista, as duas afirmações parecem incompatíveis. Mas um novo estudo mostra que elas podem ser verdadeiras ao mesmo tempo.

O Relatório Mercado de Trabalho 2027, da Gupy, conclui que a falta de mão de obra já não explica sozinha os desafios de contratação no país .

Salário, benefícios, formato de trabalho, oportunidades de crescimento, qualificação e até o avanço da inteligência artificial ajudam a entender por que empresas e candidatos continuam encontrando dificuldades para se conectar.

Elaborado a partir de milhões de registros de recrutamento, admissões e aprendizagem corporativa, o levantamento traça um retrato de um mercado de trabalho que continua aquecido, mas que se tornou mais complexo e desigual entre setores, profissões e regiões do país.

Um dos primeiros dados que chamam atenção é a redução do tempo necessário para preencher uma vaga.

O estudo mostra que o tempo médio para preencher uma vaga caiu de 37,2 dias para 23,3 dias entre janeiro de 2024 e junho de 2026. As empresas levam hoje cerca de duas semanas menos para contratar do que levavam há dois anos.

Se faltassem profissionais de forma generalizada, seria esperado que o prazo para contratar aumentasse. O que os dados mostram, porém, é um cenário mais heterogêneo.

Tempo médio para preencher uma vaga caiu de 37,2 dias para 23,3 dias entre janeiro de 2024 e junho de 2026 — Foto: Gupy

Segundo o relatório, a dificuldade para preencher vagas pode estar ligada a diferentes fatores :

💰 Salários considerados pouco competitivos;

🎁 Benefícios que não atendem às expectativas dos profissionais;

🎯 Exigências muito específicas para determinadas funções;

🚗 Distância entre residência e local de trabalho;

🏢 Modelos presenciais em setores mais disputados;

📈 Falta de perspectiva de crescimento profissional.

De acordo com a Gupy, em um mercado mais aquecido, os trabalhadores passaram a comparar mais as oportunidades antes de aceitar uma proposta .

Os benefícios também ganharam peso. Plano de saúde, vale-refeição, bônus, horários flexíveis e outras vantagens passaram a influenciar mais as decisões dos profissionais , especialmente após as mudanças observadas no mercado de trabalho nos últimos anos.

O maior desafio começa depois da contratação

Se preencher vagas continua sendo uma preocupação para muitas empresas, manter profissionais nos cargos se tornou uma tarefa igualmente importante.

O estudo mostra que 5,3% dos trabalhadores deixam a empresa em até 30 dias após a contratação . Em até três meses, esse percentual sobe para 14,1%. Em seis meses, chega a 21,4%.

Antes de completar um ano, 32,4% dos contratados já saíram da organização.

É justamente nesse ponto que entram fatores como desenvolvimento profissional e perspectiva de crescimento.

Em um mercado mais dinâmico, muitos trabalhadores não avaliam apenas o salário inicial oferecido, mas também as oportunidades de aprendizado, promoção e construção de carreira ao longo do tempo, explica a Gupy.

Apesar da aceleração no recrutamento, a etapa de admissão continua demorando. O tempo médio para concluir esse processo é de 38,5 dias, e 84,5% das admissões levam mais de sete dias para serem finalizadas.

O trabalho presencial voltou a ganhar espaço

As mudanças nas expectativas dos trabalhadores aparecem também nos modelos de trabalho.

Segundo o estudo, as contratações totalmente remotas representam atualmente 3,4% das admissões analisadas . O percentual é menor do que o observado nos anos posteriores à pandemia e reflete o retorno gradual de muitas empresas aos formatos presenciais.

🔍 A mudança ajuda a entender por que localização e deslocamento aparecem entre os fatores apontados pelo relatório.

Para muitos trabalhadores, a distância entre casa e trabalho passou a ter um peso maior na decisão de aceitar ou não uma vaga. Em grandes centros urbanos, horas gastas diariamente no trânsito podem tornar uma proposta menos atrativa, mesmo quando o salário é competitivo.

Ao mesmo tempo , vagas presenciais tendem a enfrentar mais resistência em setores onde os profissionais se acostumaram à flexibilidade do home office.

A realidade, porém, varia bastante entre os segmentos da economia. Enquanto empresas de tecnologia costumam manter maior flexibilidade, atividades como construção civil, logística, varejo e indústria continuam dependentes da presença física dos trabalhadores.

Os dados regionais reforçam a ideia de que a realidade muda bastante de um lugar para outro.

O Norte foi a região que apresentou o maior crescimento nas contratações analisadas pelo estudo, com alta de 11,8%. Já o Sul registrou retração de 7,3%. O Sudeste segue concentrando a maior parte das admissões, com 57,6% do total.

Como as contratações evoluíram em um ano — Foto: Gupy

As diferenças aparecem também quando o recorte é feito por atividade econômica.

A agropecuária liderou o crescimento das contratações, com avanço de 24%. A construção civil registrou alta de 7,5%. Já o comércio apresentou retração de 7,4%. Indústria e serviços tiveram comportamento mais estável.

Esses números mostram que os desafios enfrentados por uma empresa do agronegócio podem ser muito diferentes daqueles encontrados por uma rede varejista ou uma companhia de tecnologia.

A inteligência artificial já está mudando o perfil das vagas

Uma das transformações mais relevantes apontadas pelo levantamento envolve o avanço da inteligência artificial.

As vagas que mencionam IA cresceram 110,7% em apenas um ano , passando de cerca de 7 mil para quase 15 mil oportunidades.

Mais da metade dessas vagas está fora do setor de tecnologia.

Segundo o estudo, 59,5% das oportunidades que citam inteligência artificial aparecem em áreas como marketing, recursos humanos, administração e comercial.

As transformações tecnológicas aparecem também nas competências mais procuradas pelas empresas.

O estudo identificou crescimento da demanda por habilidades ligadas à liderança, aprendizagem contínua, resiliência e capacidade de adaptação.

A explicação é simples: ferramentas, processos e formas de trabalhar estão mudando mais rápido do que antes. Nesse cenário, empresas passaram a valorizar profissionais capazes de aprender continuamente e de acompanhar essas transformações.

O levantamento mostra ainda que posições de liderança seguem entre as mais difíceis de preencher, exigindo mais tempo para contratação do que outros tipos de vaga.

O relatório também identificou mudanças no perfil etário das contratações.

Profissionais com mais de 50 anos passaram a representar 4,65% das admissões analisadas pelo levantamento. Ao mesmo tempo, a participação dos trabalhadores com mais de 60 anos dobrou ao longo da série histórica observada.

O movimento acompanha o envelhecimento da população brasileira e sugere que trabalhadores mais experientes devem ocupar uma parcela cada vez maior do mercado de trabalho nos próximos anos.

articles.title: Cesta básica sobe em todas as capitais; tomate e carne puxam alta | G1
articles.standfirst: Por outro lado, o café em pó e o feijão ficaram mais baratos em outubro, mostra relatório do Dieese e da Conab.
articles.summary: Impulsionada por tomate e carne, a cesta básica subiu em todas as capitais e exige salário de R$ 7.992 para sustentar uma família, aponta relatório do Dieese.
articles.body:
Tomate , arroz e carne bovina de primeira foram os principais produtos responsáveis pela alta da cesta básica nas 27 capitais do país em outubro, mostra um relatório do Departamento Intersindical de Estatística e Estudos Socioeconômicos ( Dieese ) em parceria com a Companhia Nacional de Abastecimento ( Conab ), publicado no dia 10.

Por outro lado, o café em pó e o feijão ficaram mais baratos na maior parte das capitais.

De setembro para outubro, a cesta básica ficou mais cara principalmente no Nordeste , com destaque para Salvador (6,79%), Natal (6,68%) e Recife (6,41%). Apesar disso, São Paulo continuou registrando o maior custo do país, com a cesta a R$ 951,37. Na outra ponta, Aracaju teve o menor valor, de R$ 618,61. (veja os gráficos abaixo)

➡️ Com base na cesta de São Paulo, o Dieese calcula que o salário mínimo necessário para sustentar uma família de quatro pessoas seria de R$ 7.992,47 em outubro. É quase cinco vezes o mínimo em vigor, de R$ 1.621.

Valor da cesta básica por capital — Foto: g1

Quanto a cesta básica subiu nas capitais no mês de outubro de 2026. — Foto: g1

Tomate: chuva e frio atrasaram a colheita

O tomate ficou mais caro em todas as capitais entre setembro e outubro, segundo a pesquisa do Dieese e da Conab. As altas foram de 0,68%, em Boa Vista, a 58,32%, em Maceió. Em 12 meses, o preço também subiu em todas as capitais, com aumentos de 2,64%, em Macapá, a 117,12%, em Cuiabá.

A inflação oficial mostra o mesmo movimento. Segundo o Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), o tomate subiu quase 90% no ano .

Segundo João Paulo Bernardes Deleo, pesquisador da equipe de Hortifrúti do Cepea/Esalq-USP, a disparada dos preços é consequência de uma combinação de problemas climáticos.

No Sul e no Sudeste, o excesso de chuva favoreceu o surgimento de doenças nas lavouras. Já em regiões produtoras como o Cerrado Mineiro, a alternância entre períodos secos e chuvosos aumentou a incidência de pragas .

Além disso, a sequência de dias nublados reduziu a luminosidade necessária para o desenvolvimento das plantas, enquanto as temperaturas abaixo da média para a primavera atrasaram o amadurecimento dos frutos.

Com a colheita mais lenta e menos tomate chegando ao mercado, os preços avançaram ao longo dos últimos meses.

Quanto o valor da cesta básica subiu em 2026. — Foto: Arte/g1

O arroz agulhinha, o mais consumido no dia a dia, ficou mais caro em 26 capitais entre setembro e outubro. Apenas Curitiba registrou queda, de 0,23%, mostra o Dieese.

📈 As maiores altas foram observadas em Palmas (9,54%), Campo Grande (7,74%) e Fortaleza (7,18%). No acumulado de 12 meses, o produto ficou mais caro em 21 capitais, com destaque para Porto Velho (31,44%) e São Luís (23,96%).

Segundo a entidade, a alta foi influenciada pela valorização do arroz no mercado internacional e pelo avanço das exportações brasileiras. Dados do Cepea, da Esalq/USP, mostram que os embarques do cereal encerraram o primeiro semestre de 2026 no maior volume da série histórica da Secretaria de Comércio Exterior (Secex).

Com as exportações em alta , uma parte maior da safra brasileira foi vendida para outros países. Com menos arroz disponível no mercado interno, os preços subiram para os consumidores.

O preço da carne bovina de primeira subiu em 25 capitais entre setembro e outubro.

📈 As maiores altas foram registradas em São Luís (6,04%) e Rio Branco (3,54%). Houve queda apenas em Florianópolis (-0,41%) e Boa Vista (-0,13%). Em 12 meses, a carne ficou mais cara em todas as capitais pesquisadas, com aumentos que variaram de 5,93%, em Porto Alegre, a 23,94%, em Rio Branco.

Segundo o Dieese, a alta foi causada pela menor oferta de bois prontos para abate durante a entressafra, período mais seco do ano em que as pastagens perdem qualidade e os pecuaristas têm menos animais disponíveis para venda.

O Cepea aponta que esse movimento vem desde o início de 2026. A oferta de bois para abate está menor, enquanto a procura pela carne brasileira no exterior continua forte. Com menos animais disponíveis e frigoríficos disputando a compra do gado, os preços avançaram ao longo do ano.

Café: expectativa de safra maior derrubou os preços

O café em pó ficou mais barato em 20 capitais entre setembro e outubro, segundo o Dieese.

📉 As quedas variaram de 0,27%, em Florianópolis, a 6,92%, em Maceió. Em Cuiabá, o preço ficou estável. Já seis capitais registraram alta, com destaque para Macapá (1,85%). No acumulado de 12 meses, porém, o café apresentou queda em todas as capitais pesquisadas. As reduções vão de 8,72%, em Macapá, a 26,91%, em Belo Horizonte.

Segundo analistas, a principal razão para a queda é a expectativa de aumento da oferta mundial de café. No Brasil, o Cepea, da Esalq/USP, já apontava no início do ano a possibilidade de uma safra recorde em 2026/27.

No mercado internacional, o Departamento de Agricultura dos Estados Unidos (USDA) estima que a produção global da safra 2026/27 será 6% maior do que a anterior.

Quando o mercado espera uma colheita maior, cresce a perspectiva de mais café disponível para venda nos próximos meses. Com isso, os preços do grão tendem a cair, movimento que acaba chegando ao consumidor.

Como é calculado o valor da cesta básica

O custo da cesta básica é calculado todo mês pelo Dieese em parceria com a Conab, nas 27 capitais do país.

A pesquisa coleta mensalmente os preços médios cobrados no comércio pelos alimentos que compõem a cesta. O valor final é a soma do custo das quantidades definidas de cada produto, que deveriam suprir as necessidades de um trabalhador adulto durante um mês.

A composição muda conforme a região. Nas capitais do Sul, Sudeste e Centro-Oeste, a cesta tem 13 produtos. No Norte e no Nordeste, são 12: a quantidade de carne pesquisada é menor, a farinha de trigo é substituída pela de mandioca e a batata fica de fora.

articles.summary: Enquanto alguns investidores ainda tentam recuperar suas economias, outros perderam a confiança no sistema financeiro. Escândalo levou a mudanças nas regras de venda de investimentos e de proteção do FGC, mas ainda há desafios.
articles.body:
Há um ano, o Banco Central (BC) decretou a liquidação extrajudicial do Banco Master , dando início ao maior acionamento da história do Fundo Garantidor de Créditos (FGC). A estimativa inicial era de 1,6 milhão de credores e R$ 41 bilhões em garantias a serem pagas.

O escândalo, porém, ultrapassou os limites de uma crise bancária. A Polícia Federal (PF) até hoje investiga uma estrutura que teria funcionado como uma "linha de produção" de documentos falsos para inflar artificialmente o patrimônio do banco, além da venda de R$ 12,2 bilhões em carteiras de crédito que supostamente não tinham lastro ao Banco de Brasília (BRB).

As investigações também envolvem suspeitas de corrupção , lavagem de dinheiro , ameaças e invasão de dispositivos informáticos . O dono do banco, Daniel Vorcaro, está no centro de um inquérito no Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), que também envolve políticos e traz menções a ministros da própria Corte.

Longe de Brasília, o escândalo deixou marcas na vida de quem confiou suas economias à instituição. Alguns investidores recuperaram apenas parte do dinheiro aplicado e tiveram que recorrer à Justiça para tentar reaver o restante. Outros receberam os valores integralmente, mas perderam a confiança no sistema financeiro.

O g1 ouviu clientes, especialistas e representantes de órgãos reguladores para entender como a crise afetou os investidores, o que mudou no mercado financeiro e quais desafios permanecem um ano depois.

'Não sabíamos que o dinheiro estava em outro banco'

Eugênia Fernandes, de 85 anos, investiu R$ 500 mil em CDBs do Banco Master e conseguiu recuperar apenas metade do valor, coberta pelo FGC. O restante segue sem previsão de devolução. — Foto: Reprodução/g1

Eugênia Fernandes viveu por 44 anos em uma casa em Piratininga, na Região Oceânica de Niterói (RJ). Em abril de 2024, decidiu vender seu único imóvel para morar mais perto dos filhos.

A aposentadoria e a pensão, que somavam dois salários mínimos, não eram suficientes para cobrir suas despesas. Por isso, ela precisava que o dinheiro da venda gerasse uma renda mensal complementar para custear aluguel, condomínio, plano de saúde, medicamentos e outras contas.

Eugênia sempre guardou suas economias na poupança, mas decidiu investir os recursos do imóvel em um produto de investimento melhor.

Acompanhada de uma das filhas, foi até uma agência do Bradesco , onde mantém conta há quatro décadas. Segundo a família, o atendimento foi feito por um especialista do banco e por uma assessora da Ágora, corretora do grupo.

Ao todo, R$ 500 mil — praticamente todo o dinheiro disponível — foram aplicados em um único Certificado de Depósito Bancário (CDB), com vencimento em três anos e pagamento mensal de juros. O rendimento líquido era equivalente a pouco mais de dois salários mínimos por mês.

“Não sabíamos que o dinheiro estava aplicado em outro banco. Na minha cabeça, era um CDB tranquilo, feito dentro do Bradesco. Durante o atendimento, não me explicaram claramente que o investimento era do Master”, relata a aposentada.

A família só descobriu que o CDB havia sido emitido pelo Banco Master em 21 de novembro de 2025, três dias após a liquidação extrajudicial da instituição, por meio de uma mensagem enviada pela corretora por meio do WhatsApp. Até então, segundo os familiares, não havia recebido alertas da corretora sobre a situação do banco.

🛡️ A família também afirma que não houve orientação sobre os limites de cobertura do Fundo Garantidor de Créditos (FGC), que garante até R$ 250 mil por CPF e por instituição ou conglomerado financeiro, respeitado o teto global de R$ 1 milhão a cada quatro anos.

Como o valor aplicado correspondia ao dobro do limite de cobertura do FGC , pelo menos metade do dinheiro ficou fora da garantia do fundo.

Com a liquidação do Master, os pagamentos mensais de juros foram interrompidos. Sem essa renda, Eugênia passou a depender dos três filhos para arcar com despesas que variam entre R$ 7 mil e R$ 8 mil por mês.

Eugênia conta que o abalo emocional agravou problemas de saúde, que precisou passar por dois procedimentos cirúrgicos e desenvolveu um quadro de depressão.

“Eu nunca gostei de depender de ninguém, sempre criei uma vida independente. Fiz tudo isso para viver no meu canto e não depender dos meus filhos. Saber que eles agora precisam tirar deles para me sustentar é algo que me machuca muito”, desabafa.

O FGC iniciou os pagamentos aos credores do Master em 19 de janeiro de 2026 , dois meses após a quebra e depois de receber do liquidante a lista consolidada de beneficiários. Segundo o balanço mais recente, divulgado nesta semana, o FGC já havia devolvido R$ 28,8 bilhões a pouco mais de 570 mil credores do Banco Master, o equivalente a 98,89% do valor previsto e 94% dos beneficiários.

Os pagamentos também alcançaram outras instituições do conglomerado. No Master de Investimento, foram pagos R$ 11,2 bilhões a 305 mil credores. Já no Banco Pleno, o valor chegou a R$ 4,6 bilhões, distribuídos a 139 mil beneficiários.

Os números, porém, não significam que todos os investidores receberam os valores sem dificuldades. A família de Eugênia, por exemplo, teve problemas para resgatar os R$ 250 mil cobertos pelo FGC. O aplicativo do fundo não conseguia validar o documento de identificação e as imagens enviadas pela aposentada. O valor só foi liberado em fevereiro de 2026, três meses após a liquidação.

⚠️ Os outros R$ 250 mil seguem sem previsão de recuperação. Valores que ultrapassam a cobertura do FGC entram na lista de credores da instituição em liquidação. O pagamento depende dos recursos obtidos pelo liquidante, sem garantia de que o dinheiro seja recuperado integralmente.

Eugênia não ter sido informada sobre o limite de cobertura do FGC durante o atendimento é uma exceção. Ao longo do processo, uma das descobertas foi de que o uso dessa proteção como argumento para atrair investidores era uma prática comum e que preocupa especialistas.

Para Ione Amorim, economista do Instituto de Defesa do Consumidor ( Idec ), a garantia do fundo acabou incentivando a oferta de títulos com maior rentabilidade, inclusive a investidores que buscavam aplicações mais conservadoras.

“O fundo foi usado como uma espécie de cartão de crédito: assim como uma pessoa endividada recorre ao cartão para adiar o pagamento de uma dívida, a garantia foi usada para continuar captando recursos, mesmo diante dos riscos envolvidos.”

A preocupação com o uso do fundo como argumento de venda já havia levado a Associação Brasileira das Entidades dos Mercados Financeiro e de Capitais ( Anbima ) a endurecer suas regras para a distribuição de investimentos.

Em setembro de 2025, dois meses antes da liquidação do Master, entrou em vigor uma norma de autorregulação que proíbe bancos e corretoras de apresentar a proteção do FGC como principal atrativo de um produto . A regra também exige que as instituições informem claramente quem emitiu o título, quais são os riscos envolvidos e quais as condições de resgate.

Segundo Zeca Doherty, CEO da Anbima, a preocupação com esse tipo de prática já existia antes da crise, mas o episódio reforçou a necessidade de ampliar a transparência na venda de investimentos.

“O caso mostrou que um mercado que cresce e se torna mais acessível também precisa elevar seus padrões de diligência, transparência e supervisão.”

O executivo reconhece, porém, que ainda não há dados consolidados para medir se bancos e corretoras efetivamente mudaram os produtos oferecidos aos clientes.

⚖️ A família de Eugênia entrou com um processo contra a corretora Ágora, em que questiona a recomendação para que investisse em um CDB do Banco Master. Segundo a aposentada, a aplicação era incompatível com seu perfil conservador, e a corretora não prestou informações adequadas sobre os riscos do emissor, o limite de cobertura do FGC e a necessidade de diversificar os investimentos.

Procurado pelo g1 para comentar as alegações, o Bradesco informou que não comenta o caso.

A reportagem também entrou em contato com os responsáveis pela liquidação do Banco Master, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização deste texto.

Felipe Cândido teve cerca de R$ 6 mil bloqueados após a liquidação do Will Bank. Mesmo depois de recuperar o dinheiro, afirma ter perdido a confiança nos bancos digitais. — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Felipe Cândido, servidor público de 50 anos no Rio de Janeiro, não tinha investimentos em CDBs do Master. Ele mantinha cerca de R$ 6 mil em uma conta do Will Bank , banco digital controlado pelo mesmo grupo e também liquidado pelo Banco Central em janeiro de 2026.

Na época, Felipe estava afastado do trabalho por questões de saúde mental e enfrentava o luto pela morte da esposa, vítima de câncer de mama no início de 2025. Pai de quatro filhos, ele contava com o dinheiro da conta para se mudar e matricular as filhas gêmeas na escola.

Com o bloqueio, ficou sem acesso aos recursos. A energia elétrica chegou a ser cortada, e ele precisou recorrer à ajuda de amigos e vizinhos para enfrentar as dificuldades financeiras.

Felipe recebeu os R$ 6 mil de volta poucos dias após a publicação de uma reportagem do g1 sobre seu caso, mas sem juros nem correção monetária.

Com o dinheiro recuperado, quitou a dívida com um amigo que o ajudou durante o período em que ficou sem acesso à conta. Ele tentou retomar a rotina, mas os impactos emocionais da situação o levaram a se afastar novamente do trabalho por mais dois meses.

Desde então, passou a guardar suas economias na poupança da Caixa Econômica Federal. Nove meses após a primeira entrevista, Felipe contou ao g1 que perdeu a confiança nos bancos digitais.

“Voltei para a velha poupança. Não consigo mais confiar nesses bancos digitais. Eles seduzem a gente com essa promessa de ganhar um pouco mais, mas foi uma experiência traumática”, afirma.

A dificuldade para recuperar os recursos também atingiu outros clientes. Em julho, cerca de 48 mil credores do Master ainda não haviam solicitado o ressarcimento. No Will Bank, até setembro, apenas 21,24% dos clientes com valores menores a receber haviam sido pagos.

Para Ione Amorim, do Idec, parte das dificuldades está relacionada ao perfil dos usuários de bancos digitais. Muitos utilizavam as contas apenas para receber benefícios ou fazer pagamentos e podem nem saber que têm direito à devolução.

A necessidade de cadastro digital e validação da identidade por biometria também pode dificultar o acesso ao dinheiro, especialmente para consumidores mais vulneráveis.

O que mudou no comportamento dos investidores?

A decisão de Felipe de voltar à poupança mostra como a crise do Master afetou a relação de alguns investidores com o sistema financeiro. Mais do que o prejuízo ou a demora para receber os valores, episódios como esse abalaram a confiança em instituições e produtos que antes pareciam seguros.

Segundo Bruno Guimarães, planejador financeiro certificado (CFP) pela Planejar, a crise levou parte dos investidores a dar mais atenção à saúde financeira dos bancos, em vez de avaliar apenas a rentabilidade dos investimentos e a cobertura do FGC.

“Eu vejo que o investidor passou por um processo de aprendizado, de evolução e de amadurecimento, no sentido de entender a solidez do banco emissor”, afirma.

🧮 Um levantamento do Banco Central ajuda a mostrar para onde foi destinada parte dos recursos recuperados: dos R$ 37,7 bilhões ressarcidos pelo FGC entre janeiro e fevereiro de 2026, R$ 20,77 bilhões foram reaplicados em títulos emitidos por outras instituições financeiras.

Desse montante, 65,1% foram direcionados a instituições dos segmentos S1 e S2, que reúnem os bancos de maior porte e relevância para o sistema financeiro. O Master, por sua vez, integrava o segmento S3, composto por instituições menores.

Para Guimarães, os dados indicam uma possível postura mais cautelosa dos investidores em relação aos bancos de menor porte, mas não são suficientes para comprovar uma mudança generalizada de comportamento.

Ele ressalta, porém, que isso não significa que os investidores devam evitar todas essas instituições.

“A gente precisa de mais cautela e mais seletividade e, principalmente, conectar os produtos financeiros com o planejamento de cada pessoa, de cada família”, afirma.

Bancos menores enfrentam um mercado mais seletivo

Essa maior seletividade também afeta a capacidade dos bancos menores de captar recursos.

Segundo Marco Aurélio da Silva, especialista em economia e consultor empresarial, essas instituições passaram a enfrentar mais dificuldades para atrair investidores, especialmente as que dependem da oferta de CDBs com taxas elevadas.

Os dados mais recentes da Associação Brasileira de Bancos (ABBC), porém, mostram que a captação de recursos continuou avançando no setor.

No segundo trimestre de 2026, a taxa anualizada de crescimento das captações subiu de 14,5% para 18,8%.

Já o ritmo de expansão do estoque de CDBs e RDBs passou de 13,9% para 24,6%.

Segundo o especialista, os bancos menores precisam fazer um esforço maior para conquistar a confiança dos investidores, em um cenário de juros elevados e mudanças nas regras do setor.

Ao mesmo tempo, mudanças nas regras do setor buscam reduzir a dependência excessiva dos bancos em relação à garantia do FGC.

Em abril de 2026, o Conselho Monetário Nacional (CMN) aprovou a Resolução nº 5.295, que estabelece novas exigências para instituições com elevada dependência da proteção do fundo.

A norma determina que esses bancos mantenham uma parcela dos recursos em títulos públicos federais, considerados investimentos de baixo risco. A exigência entrou em vigor em julho de 2026, com percentual inicial de 5%, que aumentará gradualmente até chegar a 100% em julho de 2028, conforme os critérios da regulamentação.

O objetivo é reduzir os riscos da dependência excessiva de recursos garantidos pelo FGC, especialmente entre bancos que oferecem taxas elevadas para atrair investidores.

Para Ione Amorim, do Idec, as mudanças são importantes, mas não são suficientes para eliminar os riscos que permitiram o crescimento do Banco Master.

“O Master consolidou um crescimento astronômico, foi longe demais para voltar. Mas isso não vai impedir que outros casos, talvez menores e com impactos mais limitados, ocorram se essas medidas não forem adotadas com mais urgência.”

Os efeitos da crise do Master não ficaram restritos a quem comprou títulos do banco ou aplicou dinheiro por meio de plataformas de investimento. Instituições que administram recursos de servidores públicos também foram atingidas.

Levantamentos identificaram cerca de R$ 1,87 bilhão investido em letras financeiras do Master , títulos que não têm a proteção do FGC. Entre os maiores investidores estavam o Rioprevidência , do Rio de Janeiro, com R$ 970 milhões nessa modalidade, e a Amprev , do Amapá, com R$ 400 milhões.

A exposição total do Rioprevidência ao conglomerado chegou a aproximadamente R$ 2,6 bilhões , somando diferentes aplicações. As operações passaram a ser investigadas pela Polícia Federal.

Os problemas envolvendo o grupo também afetaram os salários de servidores públicos, desta vez por meio de outra modalidade de operação financeira.

A reportagem ouviu trabalhadores que afirmam continuar sofrendo descontos nos salários mesmo após quitar empréstimos vinculados ao Credcesta, cartão de benefício consignado associado ao grupo.

Em outubro, o governo do Rio de Janeiro publicou um decreto para suspender cobranças indevidas nos salários e benefícios de servidores ativos, aposentados e pensionistas. A medida abrange casos como descontos em duplicidade, valores superiores aos contratados, dívidas já quitadas e suspeitas de fraude.

A suspensão, porém, depende da análise de cada contrato e não garante a devolução dos valores já cobrados. Para recuperar o dinheiro, os servidores podem precisar recorrer a procedimentos administrativos ou judiciais, sem prazo definido para o ressarcimento.

A Defensoria Pública do Rio de Janeiro ajuizou uma ação civil pública em defesa dos servidores prejudicados.

Em nota ao g1 , o órgão informou que o Núcleo de Defesa do Consumidor (Nudecon) já obteve decisões judiciais para suspender a oferta de novos contratos e ampliar o atendimento aos servidores prejudicados. A devolução do dinheiro, porém, ainda depende de decisão da Justiça.

“A ação civil pública teve dois requerimentos atendidos pela Justiça: a suspensão da comercialização do cartão de benefício consignado Credcesta e a determinação de que seja criada uma central de atendimento para funcionar como canal de comunicação com os servidores prejudicados. Ainda não houve decisão judicial sobre ressarcimento às vítimas de cobranças indevidas”, informou o órgão.

As investigações sobre o conglomerado também resultaram em medidas de fiscalização e punições no mercado de capitais. Em setembro de 2026, a Comissão de Valores Mobiliários (CVM) aplicou multas superiores a R$ 200 milhões a Daniel Vorcaro , ao Banco Master, a familiares do ex-banqueiro e a outros envolvidos.

🔎 O processo, porém, nem tratou da venda de CDBs. A investigação envolveu fraudes na emissão de cotas do fundo imobiliário Brazil Realty entre 2018 e 2020, incluindo suspeitas de valorização artificial de ativos por meio de laudos falsos.

Em nota, a autarquia afirmou ter sido “o primeiro órgão de Estado a julgar um processo sancionador envolvendo o Banco Master e seus acionistas e a punir os envolvidos”. Segundo a CVM, outras apurações relacionadas ao caso continuam em andamento.

“A autarquia segue conduzindo apurações em processos relacionados ao caso, ao mesmo tempo em que trabalha para fortalecer os procedimentos de supervisão, fiscalização e investigação de possíveis ilícitos”, informou.

O que mudou após a crise do Master — e o que ainda falta fazer?

Um ano após a liquidação do Banco Master, algumas medidas para reforçar a proteção dos investidores já estão em vigor, enquanto outras ainda precisam ser implementadas.

Entre as principais mudanças e iniciativas estão:

Captação bancária: a Resolução nº 5.295, aprovada pelo CMN em abril de 2026, estabeleceu novas exigências para instituições com elevada dependência do FGC, com implementação gradual.

Proteção dos investidores: a Consulta Pública 131/2026 do Banco Central propõe que instituições financeiras priorizem o melhor interesse dos clientes e ampliem a transparência sobre comissões recebidas na venda de investimentos. A consulta está prevista para permanecer aberta até janeiro de 2027, com entrada em vigor das regras proposta para 2028.

Fiscalização do mercado: a CVM editou duas resoluções em 2026. A Resolução 245 tornou mais rígidos os controles de prevenção à lavagem de dinheiro em determinadas operações com investidores estrangeiros. Já a Resolução 247 ampliou o envio de informações sobre operações de crédito ao Banco Central, para facilitar o acompanhamento de riscos.

Apesar das mudanças, a liquidação do Master também levantou dúvidas sobre a capacidade do FGC de enfrentar novas crises bancárias.

Para recompor os recursos utilizados nos ressarcimentos, os bancos anteciparam R$ 32 bilhões em contribuições. Em junho de 2026, o FGC tinha patrimônio de R$ 115,9 bilhões , equivalente a 2,02% do total de depósitos cobertos pelo fundo, abaixo da meta de 2,5% estabelecida pela própria instituição.

Na avaliação de Bruno Guimarães, o fundo cumpriu seu papel de ajudar a preservar a estabilidade do sistema financeiro, mas precisou fazer um esforço inédito para cobrir os prejuízos.

“Precisamos pensar no que aconteceria diante de uma crise simultânea em várias instituições. O FGC não teria recursos para cobrir todos os depósitos do sistema de uma só vez.”

Para Zeca Doherty, da Anbima, o episódio também expôs os limites dos mecanismos de fiscalização diante de suspeitas de fraude.

“O Master foi um caso de fraude. Mesmo os mecanismos mais rigorosos de controle não estão imunes à atuação de pessoas mal-intencionadas com objetivo deliberado de burlar regras.”

articles.title: 'Srinivasan, Singh selectively picking facts': Ex-Tata Trusts trustee Khambata
articles.summary: MUMBAI: \"What takes the cake is your suggestion that I strategised to 'temporarily oust' Venu as a trustee to alter the Trusts' constitution.\" With that
articles.body: MUMBAI: "What takes the cake is your suggestion that I strategised to 'temporarily oust' Venu as a trustee to alter the Trusts' constitution." With that line, former Tata Trusts trustee Darius Khambata escalated an already bitter governance battle at the apex of the Tata Group, rejecting allegations that he sought to exploit Venu Srinivasan's brief absence from the Trusts to reshape its structure.In a sharp rejoinder to vice-chairmen Srinivasan and Vijay Singh, Khambata accused his former colleagues of selectively recounting events and failing to explain the abrupt reversal of their position on a Tata Sons listing.Khambata also defended the Trusts' control of Tata Sons, questioned the handling of the succession process involving company chairman N 'Chandra' Chandrasekaran and rejected suggestions that he had acted in concert with Trusts chairman Noel Tata.'Safeguarding Trusts' stake in Tata Sons rests with trustees'Former Tata Trusts trustee Darius Khambata said Venu Srinivasan's failure to secure reappointment in Oct 2025 stemmed from former trustee Mehli Mistry's interpretation of an Oct 17, 2024 resolution under which trustees agreed to support one another's reappointment. Mistry's position was based on whether Srinivasan had honoured that commitment and Khambata had "no involvement" in the decision.Khambata also noted that at the Nov 11, 2025 meeting where he proposed Noel's son Neville Tata as a trustee, Singh had proposed Bhaskar Bhat in what he described as a "mirror image" of his own move. If Neville's appointment was evidence of a strategy to take advantage of Srinivasan's absence, he argued, the same charge could apply to Singh's backing of Bhat.Khambata also cited his own voting record, noting that he supported Srinivasan's reappointment in Oct and Nov 2025 despite having the ability to block it.He further alleged that Srinivasan, Singh and Noel had themselves failed to abide by the Oct 17, 2024 resolution when they voted against Mistry's reappointment. He said Srinivasan and Singh had not objected to the departures of Pramit Jhaveri and Khambata himself from the Trusts.Listing remained at the centre of his criticism. Srinivasan and Singh "still give no reason for changing your minds" after backing the anti-listing stance of Tata Sons and Trusts in March 2024, May 2025 and July 2025, only to execute a "volte-face" in April 2026, he said.Rejecting suggestions that his defence of the Tata model amounted to support for control by Noel, he wrote that "all trustees are equal" and that responsibility for safeguarding Trusts' stake in Tata Sons rested collectively with trustees rather than any individual. He dismissed arguments that such oversight could affect the Trusts' tax-exempt status.Khambata reopened questions around the succession process involving Chandrasekaran. He maintained there was no contradiction between supporting Chandrasekaran's third term in 2025 and later criticising Tata Sons board's actions in Sept 2026, describing Chandrasekaran's performance as "excellent". His criticism, he said, was directed at the manner in which the board acted in Sept 2026 rather than the chairman himself.Pushing back against claims that he had remained silent as uncertainty grew over Chandrasekaran's future, Khambata said he wrote to co-trustees on March 2, 2026, seeking discussions after media reports on the Feb 2026 Tata Sons board meeting. "No trustee responded. Was I to hold a meeting by myself?" he wrote.According to Khambata, trustees later agreed on Aug 13, 2026, to respect Chandrasekaran's decision not to seek another term and begin constituting a selection committee for a successor. He questioned whether Srinivasan, as a Trust nominee director, had drawn Tata Sons' attention to that position before its nominations committee moved to ask Chandrasekaran to continue.Khambata also rejected suggestions that he lacked independence, saying he had differed with Noel on "several major issues" during 2025 and 2026, while Srinivasan and Singh had themselves agreed with Noel on many of those matters before later breaking ranks. Suggesting that criticism of him stemmed from his decision to "call out" the Sept 17 Tata Sons board meeting, he described the allegations against him as a personal attack.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Thane man buys Rs 72 lakh flat jointly with wife, faces Rs 14.25 lakh tax addition at steep rate as taxman cites developer’s Gmail and Yahoo emails containing alleged ‘on-money’ receipts; why ITAT Mumbai gave property buyer full relief
articles.summary: When you buy a property, it is very important to keep all records of transactions and payments.
articles.body: When you buy a property, it is very important to keep all records of transactions and payments. In case of an Income Tax Department query, documents form an important part of your defence.The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Mumbai, has deleted a Rs 14.25 lakh addition made against a Thane flat buyer after the Income Tax Department alleged that he had paid money over and above the consideration recorded in the property agreement.The tribunal observed that the Income Tax Department had failed to establish any link between the buyer and the alleged ‘on-money’ transaction. Read on to know what happened.What the case is aboutThe dispute involved a man who purchased a flat in Thane, jointly with his wife for Rs 72 lakh. The property was registered in April 2012.The man filed his income tax return for assessment year 2012-13, declaring income of Rs 2,71,280. The return was initially accepted, but the assessment was subsequently reopened after the department received information concerning alleged cash payments to the real estate developer from whom the flat had been bought.According to the assessing officer, material associated with the group’s Gmail and Yahoo accounts contained details of alleged ‘on-money’ receipts.The officer also referred to an Excel sheet said to contain flat-wise and shop-wise details of cash payments. Statements by the group’s sales head, and one of its promoters, were also cited.On this basis, the officer alleged that the man in this case had paid additional cash for the flat.Acting on information shared by the investigation wing, the assessing officer alleged that the taxpayer had paid Rs 28.5 lakh in cash during the financial year 2011-12.Since he held a 50% share in the property, the officer treated Rs 14.25 lakh as unexplained money and added the amount to his taxable income, making it liable to tax at a steep rate.The man disputed the allegation. His representative submitted that he and his wife had purchased the flat for Rs 72 lakh and that the payments were reflected in the transaction records and registered agreement dated April 4, 2012. The taxpayer also produced a confirmation from the builder acknowledging receipt of Rs 72 lakh.The taxpayer argued that the department had not supplied the material allegedly establishing the cash payment.He also challenged the use of third-party statements without an opportunity to cross-examine the people who made them.The Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) upheld the addition and declined his request for cross-examination, prompting the appeal before the tribunal.Why ITAT Mumbai ruled in favour of property buyerMumbai ITAT bench found that the Rs 14.25 lakh addition to the taxpayer’s income was based largely on statements recorded from the developer’s officials and references to electronic material purportedly seized during the search.The bench pointed out that the alleged incriminating documents had neither been submitted as part of the case records nor provided to the taxpayer. It also noted that the Gmail and Yahoo mail records cited by the Income Tax Department were not produced during the assessment proceedings.The order states: “Copy of incriminating material or the material contained in the alleged Gmail or yahoo mail is neither brought on record no supplied to the assessee.”The tribunal observed that the taxpayer had denied paying any cash over and above the declared price and had submitted a confirmation from the builder acknowledging receipt of Rs 72 lakh for the flat.The tribunal also noted that the lower authorities had not taken account of the builder’s confirmation acknowledging receipt of Rs 72 lakh. It observed: “No cognizance of confirmation of builder was taken by AO or the ld CIT(A).”Cross-examination was another central issue. The man had challenged the use of statements made by third parties without being allowed to question them. The tribunal stated: “Statement per se cannot be considered as evidence, against third party unless it is tested by cross examination.”The tribunal also considered earlier ITAT decisions involving similar additions against buyers of properties linked to the same real estate group.In those cases, additions based on statements without adequate corroboration had been deleted.Following those decisions, it concluded that the addition against the man was not sustainable because the assessing officer had failed to substantiate the alleged payment with incriminating material.It therefore deleted the Rs 14.25 lakh addition.Tax experts said the ruling could affect several disputes arising from searches of real estate developers, particularly cases involving allegations of ‘on-money’ payments.According to them, the decision strengthens the position of taxpayers facing such additions. It also underscores that the income-tax department must establish, using credible evidence that can be independently verified, that a particular buyer paid cash beyond the declared sale consideration. Without such evidence, these additions could face difficulties in withstanding scrutiny at the appellate stage.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.summary: Mumbai: India's retail credit portfolio grew 18.8% year-on-year to Rs 185.2 lakh crore in Sept 2026, led by strong growth in gold loans and consumer
articles.body: Mumbai: India's retail credit portfolio grew 18.8% year-on-year to Rs 185.2 lakh crore in Sept 2026, led by strong growth in gold loans and consumer durable loans, although early signs of stress emerged in select lending segments, according to a report by CRIF Credit Information Services.Outstanding gold loans rose 60.6% to Rs 23.3 lakh crore, making them the main driver of retail credit growth. Retail credit expanded 18% during the period, making it the fastest-growing segment for lenders. Consumer durable loans recorded the fastest growth among major consumption-linked categories, rising 44.5% year-on-year and 6.3% sequentially to Rs 1.3 lakh crore.The report also pointed to emerging signs of stress in select portfolios. Delinquencies in the 91-180-day bucket for personal loans increased to 1.1% in Sept 2026 from 0.8% in June. In gold loans, delinquencies in the 31-90-day bucket rose to 1.3% from 0.9% over the same period.Secured business loans grew 45.2% to Rs 19.6 lakh crore, while auto loans increased 18.2% to Rs 10.2 lakh crore. Personal loans rose 13.8% to Rs 17.5 lakh crore and housing loans grew 10.4% to Rs 46.4 lakh crore. However, outstanding two-wheeler loans contracted 5.2% sequentially.Gold loan originations by value increased 27.2% year-on-year to Rs 8.2 lakh crore in Q2 FY27, even as the number of loans originated declined 4.1%. The average ticket size rose 32.7% to Rs 2.2 lakh. Loans of Rs 5 lakh and above accounted for 40.3% of originations by value while representing around 10% of volumes.Southern states continued to account for more than 70% of the gold loan portfolio. Sequentially, origination volumes remained almost stagnant while their value increased 1.9%. Consumer durable loans also recorded an increase in 91-180-day delinquencies among NBFCs and loans below Rs 50,000. In the two-wheeler segment, early signs of stress remained concentrated in NBFC portfolios and loans below Rs 1 lakh.Premiumisation was evident across several lending categories, with higher-value loans accounting for a growing share of originations.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Intel cuts more jobs as CEO Lip-Bu Tan's efficiency push continues
articles.summary: After a series of layoffs over the last two years, Intel has laid off workers again.
articles.body:
Intel has laid off workers again, adding to a series of cuts this year.

The job cuts add to a lengthy restructuring at the US chipmaker.

Ongoing Intel restructuring has been focused on cutting management layers and refocusing projects.

After a series of layoffs over the last two years, Intel has let workers go again in another round of cuts.

The cuts are the latest sign that CEO Lip-Bu Tan's effort to make the chipmaker leaner is continuing into the final months of the year.

This week, employees shared on social media about being affected by layoffs in Intel's global IT workforce.

"As part of our broader strategy to become a more focused and efficient company, we continually assess our workforce to ensure priorities and resources are appropriately aligned," an Intel spokesperson said in a statement to Business Insider.

Intel did not disclose how many employees were affected or identify the teams involved.

The job cuts add to a lengthy restructuring at the US chipmaker, which has reduced its workforce and trimmed projects as it tries to revive its business after years of manufacturing setbacks and market share losses in AI chips. Intel has done several small rounds of layoffs this year.

Tan, who became Intel's CEO last year, has said his restructuring plan was designed to lower expenses, reduce management layers, and shift resources away from lower-priority initiatives.

Intel employed 81,100 people at the end of September, down from 85,100 at the end of 2025, according to company filings.

Its headcount has fallen sharply since 2024, when Intel announced plans to cut more than 15,000 jobs, or about 15% of its workforce, under then-CEO Pat Gelsinger .

articles.title: Nvidia enters the post-Jensen Huang era with a bang
articles.summary: Nvidia delivered a message with its first earnings report under new leadership: The sky isn’t falling.
articles.body: Nvidia delivered a message with its first earnings report under new leadership: The sky isn’t falling. With a new CEO and board chair just days after the resignation of co-founder Jensen Huang, the company reported results Tuesday that beat analysts’ expectations for AI chip sales. Nvidia’s new leaders also appeared to calm some investors’ nerves about the immediate future of a company at the heart of the AI economy. Colette Kress, the interim CEO and Nvidia’s longtime chief financial officer, and Harvey Jones, the newly elected board chair, used the quarterly earnings call to answer many — but not all — of the biggest questions hanging over Nvidia, including who will be running things in the near term. Just hours before the earnings release, Huang had injected fresh uncertainty into precisely that question when announced that he would be “honored” to return to the job of CEO, if the company’s board decided to bring him back. At the top of Tuesday’s call, Jones shot down that idea. “The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” he said. “While this was an unexpected transition, the board acted deliberately and in the best interest of the company’s employees, customers, partners and shareholders.” Following the earnings call, Kress poured even more cold water on the idea of Huang’s return. “Jensen resigned from his position with Nvidia, and the board accepted his resignation,” she said in an interview with CNBC. “The board has determined that they will not reinstate Jensen, and that is our statement and what the board has decided to do.” Huang resigned Thursday after reports that he had multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a woman believed to be spying for China and another with an executive who reported to him. On Tuesday morning, Huang said he had made “serious mistakes in my personal life.” Jones said the board would consider both internal and external candidates for CEO and had hired an executive search firm, Heidrick & Struggles, to help with the process. He also endorsed Kress as interim CEO, saying that she had been “instrumental in executing strategy” and possessed a “deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position.” Investors responded positively to the earnings report and the call, sending Nvidia’s share price higher by 5% in after-hours trading. Nonetheless, the stock is still trading about 30% below the all-time high it reached last month. The bullishness on Wall Street was driven in part by the company’s financial results. Revenue for the three months ending Oct. 25 was $115.8 billion — more than double the revenue for the same period a year earlier. Adjusted earnings per share were $2.68, also more than double a year earlier. Kress also announced that Nvidia was raising its forecast for future sales from the previous estimate of 70% revenue growth over the next year, up to 75%. “We are addressing strong demand for compute across a diverse and expansive set of end customers,” she said. Kress singled out demand coming from the frontier AI companies that are developing new models — such as Anthropic and OpenAI — and said they’d been demanding more chips, “even in the last week.” This is all despite the headwinds confronting AI chip sales right now, such as China-related export controls, public pushback against data centers and the radioactive politics of AI. Nvidia’s optimistic guidance was “the most important line in the release,” wrote veteran tech analyst Dan Ives, a managing director at Yorkville Ives consultancy. “There was a real chance a board five days into an interim CEO would hold back a formal outlook, and instead Kress put a number above the Street,” he wrote in a note to clients, referring to her forecast that exceeded what Wall Street analysts had been expecting. Kress’ guidance “speaks volumes about the backlog she inherited” of demand for Nvidia’s chips. A few of Kress’ answers to analysts’ questions were less specific, or convincing, than others. Asked whether incoming Democratic majorities in Congress would slow down AI development next year, she said the industry would need to work together with individual communities and the government. “We’re always going to be engaged with the government, making sure that we are all aligned in terms of what we see in terms of the future.” AI and data center companies, she said, will need to ensure that “communities understand the jobs that are going to be newly available.” But it’s not clear that the promise of future jobs will be enough to turn the tide of public opinion in favor of data centers. Earlier this month, 40 out of the 41 data center ballot initiatives put to voters were rejected. At another point, Kress was asked about new rules from the Commerce Department restricting the sale of advanced AI chips to several countries that have been major sources of revenue for Nvidia in recent years. The company would “spend some time studying” the new rules, she said, but she did not believe they would affect overall sales because demand from other customers was so strong. How long this AI euphoria will last, though, is unclear. Several large companies have recently announced plans to limit their spending on AI services and tokens, questioning whether the technology is delivering the huge returns it promised. Meanwhile, the number of individuals who use chatbots is growing but the lion’s share of those users don’t pay for advanced computing power. And polls consistently show that more Americans believe AI’s impact on society will be negative, than think it will be positive.

articles.title: Nvidia dismisses calls to reinstate Jensen Huang amid blockbuster earnings
articles.summary: Nvidia board chair says chip giant ‘does not intend’ to reinstate Huang as it projects revenues of $130bn in Q4.
articles.body:
Nvidia has shot down the prospect of Jensen Huang returning as CEO amid the chip giant’s latest blockbuster earnings results.

Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones said on Tuesday during an earnings call that the company had no plans to reinstate Huang following his “voluntary resignation” for “personal behaviour inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms”.

“The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” Jones said.

Jones, appointed Nvidia’s first-ever board chair after Huang’s resignation last week, made his comments as Nvidia continued its run of stellar earnings in the third quarter.

Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8bn in the quarter that ended October 25, up 103 percent year-on-year. Net profit came in at $64.9bn, up 109 percent year-on-year.

Nvidia, currently led by interim CEO Colette Kress while its board seeks a permanent replacement, said it expected next quarter revenue to reach $130bn, plus or minus 3 percent.

“Earnings were very strong, and were just what the market needed to shake off some AI-related jitters experienced over the last couple of weeks,” Will Rhind, chief executive officer at GraniteShares Advisors, told Al Jazeera.

“The earnings call, of course without Jensen, was a signal for the bulls that life carries on without him and the foundation the company has built is as robust as ever,” Rhind said.

Huang resigned amid scrutiny of his relationship with a tech executive accused of being a Chinese intelligence operative or asset. He said earlier on Tuesday he would be “honoured” to return if the board deemed it in the best interests of shareholders and the company.

Nearly 200,000 people have added their names to an open letter calling for Huang’s reinstatement, including Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney.

Shares of Nvidia, which have fallen more than 30 percent over the past month, closed down 0.4 percent on Tuesday, before rising 4.8 percent in after-hours trading.

Nvidia has been under intense scrutiny over its relationship with the Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, suspected of diverting advanced chips to China in violation of US export controls.

On Monday, the US Department of Commerce and the Department of Justice confirmed that prosecutors had opened a criminal investigation into Megaspeed.

President Donald Trump’s administration also moved on Monday to close a legal loophole that had allowed Chinese AI developers to access advanced chips remotely at data centres in third countries.

The rule issued by the Bureau of Industry and Security designates Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil as export destinations with an “unacceptable risk of diversion” and requires anyone seeking to ship advanced chips to those countries to obtain an export licence.

Jay Goldberg, senior analyst at Seaport Research Partners in San Francisco, said investors will closely watch how the clampdown on China’s access to high-end chips affects Nvidia’s business.

“I think they had a good quarter and guidance, in particular, raising their revenue forecast for next year,” Goldberg told Al Jazeera.

“But not sure how much of that matters until we get more clarity on who the next CEO will be and just how much exposure they really have to PRC AI companies,” Goldberg said, using the acronym for the People’s Republic of China, the country’s official name.

“As for their comments about Jensen returning, I think they said what they had to say. The board has to navigate a lot of legal guardrails. I think it is still possible for Jensen to return. Unlikely but possible.”

Megaspeed, whose former executive Alice Huang had an intimate relationship with Jensen Huang and has been accused of working with China’s Ministry of State Security, has denied wrongdoing, saying media reports about its operations were “not supported by verifiable evidence”.

Alice Huang has not publicly commented on the claims of espionage, which have been circulated in the media by unnamed US officials.

Beijing has denied the spying allegations, calling them “entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China”.

articles.title: Oil prices today: Crude falls as US inventories rise; Iran tensions limit losses
articles.summary: Oil prices declined on Wednesday after industry data showed a sharp increase in US crude and fuel inventories last week, although continued hostilities
articles.body: Oil prices declined on Wednesday after industry data showed a sharp increase in US crude and fuel inventories last week, although continued hostilities between the United States and Iran and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz limited the fall.US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures dropped 56 cents, or 0.65%, to $85.45 a barrel, while Brent crude futures fell 16 cents, or 0.17%, to $92.98 a barrel as of 1.49 am GMT, according to Reuters.Market sources said US crude stocks increased by 5.28 million barrels in the week ended November 13, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) released on Tuesday.Gasoline inventories rose by 5.12 million barrels, while distillate stocks increased by 351,000 barrels.The inventory build put pressure on prices, but concerns over supply disruptions in the Middle East continued to support the market.US-Iran conflict keeps supply concerns aliveOil benchmarks had settled higher on Tuesday as the conflict between Washington and Tehran intensified, despite continuing talks involving Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar.Bahrain's defence force said on Wednesday it had intercepted Iranian aerial attacks on the country, which hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. The development followed an exchange of strikes between the US and Iran a day earlier.Iranian drones attacked a US military radar system in Bahrain on Tuesday, prompting Washington to strike a missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island, Reuters reported.Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has also faced continued risks. An LPG tanker was hit by a projectile while sailing through the waterway off Oman's coast on Monday, forcing its crew to evacuate.The strait is a key route for global energy shipments, and attacks on vessels have added to concerns over the movement of oil and other fuel supplies.“Although regional supply may continue to recover through alternative routes, the latest vessel data suggests that normalization of flows through Hormuz is still not possible under current conditions,” LSEG analysts said in a note on Tuesday.Houthi drone claims add to regional risksSupply concerns have also extended beyond the immediate US-Iran confrontation. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi group said on Tuesday that it had launched five drones towards two pumping stations along Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline.Saudi Arabia has been using the pipeline during the conflict to reroute oil to its Yanbu port for export, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.The latest developments have kept attention on the security of alternative export routes as the conflict continues, even as rising US crude and fuel inventories weigh on prices.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Dollar hovers near 19-month high as December Fed rate hike bets gather pace
articles.summary: The US dollar remained close to a 19-month high on Wednesday as steady retail sales, rising import prices and comments from Federal Reserve officials
articles.body: The US dollar remained close to a 19-month high on Wednesday as steady retail sales, rising import prices and comments from Federal Reserve officials strengthened expectations of another interest rate hike in December.The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, edged up 0.05% to 103.66 after touching 103.78 overnight, its highest level since April 2, 2025.The euro slipped 0.12% to $1.0984, while the Japanese yen weakened 0.06% to 159.46 per dollar. Sterling also lost 0.06% to trade at $1.32.US retail sales rose 0.2% in October, matching market expectations, while import prices increased 1.1%, against forecasts of a 0.7% rise. The figures reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates by 25 basis points next month. Traders are pricing in such a move, according to the CME FedWatch tool."Overall, the report reinforces our view that further interest rate hikes from the Fed are warranted in order to counter demand-pull inflation," Henry Russell, a London-based economist for ANZ, said about the US sales data. "The strength of domestic demand in the US, in our view, warrants a decisive monetary policy response from the Fed."Investors are awaiting US housing starts data for October, due later on Wednesday. Analysts expect the figure to increase to 1.245 million from 1.221 million in September, while building permits are projected to decline.Federal Reserve officials' comments will also be in focus. New York Fed President John Williams, who said on Tuesday that further rate increases would likely be needed to tackle high inflation, is expected to speak again. Fed Board Governor Michael Barr and Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari are also scheduled to address separate events. The central bank's meeting minutes from last month, when it kept rates unchanged, are due on Thursday.Meanwhile, the yen weakened despite Japan reporting a 20.5% year-on-year increase in exports in October, beating the 20% market forecast. Exports rose for the 14th consecutive month, reaching a record monthly value on strong semiconductor demand. The growth followed a 16.5% increase in September.The Australian dollar was little changed at $0.673 after touching its weakest level since January 19, while the New Zealand dollar gained 0.05% to $0.5495, recovering slightly from a 19-month low recorded on Tuesday.Broader market sentiment remained cautious following a selloff in AI and technology stocks, driven by Nvidia CEO's sudden departure, a Democratic sweep in US midterm elections and concerns over debt-funded AI infrastructure expansion.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Root cause of US aviation shutdown not yet determined, Duffy says
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, Nov 17 (Reuters) - US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Tuesday that no root cause had yet been determined for the router that failed o...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Nov 17 (Reuters) - US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Tuesday that no root cause had yet been determined for the router that failed on Friday, ‌triggering a nationwide aviation shutdown and more than 18,000 flight cancellations.

Duffy said it remained unclear why ‌L3Harris Technologies' installation of a router in a remote El Dorado, Arkansas, facility had a big enough impact on the network ​to lead to a nearly five-hour aviation ground stop that affected hundreds of thousands of airline passengers.

"We've been able to recreate what happened in El Dorado, but the root cause of what happened, we don't have clarity yet," Duffy told reporters after a meeting with senators.

The swap was part of a routine switchover from ‌copper wire to digital fiber to modernize ⁠equipment, and FAA head Bryan Bedford told reporters that speculation that AI was involved in the outage was unfounded.

Duffy said the installation of 68 prior routers, which ⁠are made by Hewlett Packard Enterprise-owned Juniper Networks, had not led to any issues. But he said the FAA has paused installations of Juniper routers as testing continues at an L3Harris laboratory in Florida with the FAA, ​Cisco and ​the FBI on site.

L3Harris has said it is cooperating ​with the official investigation into what went ‌wrong.

Duffy said that during the Biden administration, the FAA replaced 19% of its telecom network from copper to fiber and in one year the Trump administration has replaced just over 50%. "We do have to get this work done. Otherwise, staying on the old system for longer is going to mean more risk," he said.

L3Harris had been installing Juniper routers to replace Cisco routers, produced in 2001, which were supposed to have been replaced ‌in 2006, the FAA said.

Duffy said the FAA had spent ​a year at its tech center testing the Juniper routers, ​but the installation at the Arkansas radio ​communications site led to an overload of a key government communications system. That destabilized ‌aircraft communications and radar feeds, affecting 17 of ​22 FAA en route ​air traffic control centers.

After the incident, the broadcasting function was also disabled on all the new routers as well as 60 other routers in the system as a precaution, the FAA said.

Juniper ​owner HPE said it believed its ‌equipment was working as configured. "The FAA is assessing the configuration and performance of all infrastructure ​involved to determine the cause," the company said.

(Reporting by David Shepardson, Daphne Psaledakis and ​Christian Martinez; Editing by Caitlin Webber and Jamie Freed)

articles.title: Nepal to buy up to 350 MW power from India as hydropower output falls
articles.summary: India has granted Nepal permission to import up to 350 MW of electricity during the winter season to meet its domestic demand.
articles.body: India has granted Nepal permission to import up to 350 MW of electricity during the winter season to meet its domestic demand. The approval comes as the country’s hydropower generation declined and several power projects remain damaged by recent floods.The central electricity authority (CEA), under India's ministry of power, has authorised the Nepal electricity authority (NEA), the state-owned power utility, to purchase electricity from the Indian energy exchange (IEX) at competitive rates for up to 17 hours daily, NEA officials said.NEA managing direction Dirghayu Kumar Shrestha said that the approval will remain valid from November 17, 2026, to July 31, 2027. The move is expected to help Nepal bridge the seasonal gap between electricity demand and domestic production, according to news agency PTI.Under the approved arrangement, Nepal can import 300 MW through the Kataiya-Kushaha, Ramnagar-Surajpura and Raxaul-Parwanipur transmission lines. An additional 50 MW can be sourced through the new nautanwa-mainahiya transmission line.Nepal's heavy reliance on run-of-the-river hydropower projects makes its electricity production dependent on seasonal changes in river flows.During summer, increased water levels allow the country to generate surplus electricity, much of which is exported to India. However, falling river levels during winter reduce hydropower output, compelling Nepal to depend on electricity imports to meet domestic requirements.The country's power generation capacity has also been affected by damage to several hydropower projects in central Nepal during the devastating Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi floods in August.Power projects with a combined installed capacity of 431 MW have remained disconnected from the national grid since the disaster, further straining domestic electricity supplies.However, officials expect domestic generation to recover from mid-April as river water levels begin to rise. The improvement could reduce Nepal's reliance on imported electricity and potentially enable the country to resume power exports.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones?
