articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has announced a \"very big trade deal\" with the Philippines, alongside plans to expand defence, nuclear energy and broader energy
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has announced a "very big trade deal" with the Philippines, alongside plans to expand defence, nuclear energy and broader energy cooperation between the two countries.Speaking during his state visit to Manila on Wednesday, Trump described the trade agreement as a "magnificent deal" that would be fair to both sides.The announcement came during Trump's meeting with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, where the two leaders discussed strengthening their existing defence partnership and exploring new areas of cooperation.US expands defence support, explores nuclear energy projectTrump had earlier said that Washington had expanded military support for the Philippines, approving more than $5 billion in arms sales.He also raised the possibility of working with Manila on a major civilian nuclear energy project, suggesting that the country could adopt American technology for its first modern nuclear project."For the Philippines to embrace American technology in its first modern nuclear project would underscore the strength of the important relationship, and we're probably going to do something very big to do with nuclear," Trump said.Energy cooperation could also extend beyond nuclear power. Trump said the Philippines could become a partner in a planned natural gas export project in Alaska, adding that discussions on wider energy cooperation were already under way."The Philippines would be a very natural partner in this effort. We are working on that," he said.Trump’s series of visitsTrump's visit to Manila began on Tuesday and is part of a three-day trip that will take him to China for the APEC summit. The Philippine capital is his first overseas destination since his party suffered significant losses in the midterm elections.The visit comes as Trump seeks to formalise trade arrangements and engage with regional partners, while facing several challenges at home, including a major disruption to the US aviation industry and a scandal that has shaken the global AI industry.Alongside his discussions with the Philippines, Trump signed a trade statement with Thailand, continuing his efforts to strike trade agreements since launching a trade war last year, backed by steep tariff threats.After completing his engagements in Manila, Trump is scheduled to travel to China for the APEC summit. articles.title: GTA VI has made more than $1.5 billion before anyone has played it
articles.summary: It’s been a long road back to Vice City. Here’s a look back at Grand Theft Auto since the last game, and how we got here.
articles.body: Grand Theft Auto VI is set to be one of the biggest entertainment launches ever when it is released on November 19. The latest game in the Grand Theft Auto (GTA) franchise has had several delays along the way, but after 13 years – the longest gap between releases in the franchise’s history – it is finally here. As fans prepare to return to Leonida – Rockstar Games’ fictionalized version of Florida, where they will steal cars, rob businesses and spend their ill-gotten gains – here’s a look at the popular franchise since the last release. The wait hasn’t put players off. Pre-orders of the game are estimated to already have surpassed $1.5 billion, according to market intelligence firm Sensor Tower. Compared to other recent game releases the scale of GTA VI is unmatched. Nine days before launch GTA VI broke $1 billion in pre-order revenue — almost twice what Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II, the best-selling game in the US in 2022, had made at the same time before its launch. The previous game, Grand Theft Auto V, was a huge success, becoming the bestselling game of 2013, and has continued to generate hundreds of millions of dollar for the franchise every year. The long success has been in part thanks to GTA online – an online multiplayer expansion of the game launched a few weeks after GTA V was released. GTA Online allows players to join others to continue exploring Los Santos – a fictionalized version of Los Angeles – after having completed the game. GTA Online also allowed Rockstar Games to generate revenue in more ways than just buying the game. New content and game modes have kept players coming back and fans can pay real world money for in-game extras or upgrades. GTA Online alone has made over $5 billion dollars in the last decade. This continued interest has contributed to GTA becoming one of the biggest game franchises ever. Top selling games include the 1984 classic Tetris, 1990s bestseller Pokémon, and the more recent first-person shooter franchise Call of Duty. Grand Theft Auto is only 40 million copies away from the top spot, so who knows how this list will look after tomorrow’s launch. After 13 years, the wait is almost over.

articles.title: Asia stocks cling to gains after Nvidia earnings as Anthropic pricing looms
articles.summary: By Gregor Stuart Hunter SINGAPORE, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Stocks eked out a small advance in Asia on Wednesday after Nvidia posted a better-than-expected sales f...
articles.body:
SINGAPORE, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Stocks eked out a small advance in Asia on Wednesday after Nvidia posted a better-than-expected sales forecast amid uncertainty about company's future leadership, while oil prices dropped after data showed rising US inventories.

In choppy trade, MSCI's ‌broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was up 0.1%, narrowly on track to break a four-day losing streak. Japan's Nikkei 225 ‌gained 0.3% after several reversals, while US S&P 500 e-mini futures held gains throughout the trading day, up 0.2%.

"Nvidia's results were reassuring and gave investors a reason to refocus on earnings, but ​they haven't resolved the broader questions around AI spending returns, financing sustainability and leadership uncertainty," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Bank in Singapore.

"So we are seeing an initial relief rally, but not necessarily the conviction needed for a sustained recovery."

In oil markets, Brent crude futures were 1.1% lower at $92.16 a barrel in Asian trade following data showing an increase in US crude and fuel inventories last week, although the ongoing Middle East conflict and disruptions to shipping through ‌the Strait of Hormuz limited losses.

Nvidia shares ⁠initially jumped in after-hours trading after the chipmaker, seen as a bellwether for the AI sector, reported both third-quarter revenue and a fourth-quarter forecast that beat market expectations in its first earnings report since Jensen Huang's abrupt departure as CEO ⁠this month.

But the shares pared earlier gains to 0.3% in after-hours trading on Blue Ocean.

The Wall Street Journal reported the SEC is probing Nvidia, citing people familiar with the matter. The SEC declined to comment.

"We're at a point of peak uncertainty because investors still don't know what Nvidia's long-term leadership will look like," said Brian ​Colello, ​senior equity analyst at Morningstar.

Overnight, stocks on Wall Street sold off again, with the ​S&P 500 down 1% to log a fourth consecutive fall prior ‌to Nvidia's earnings report.

In early European trade, pan-region futures were flat, German DAX futures were down 0.2% and FTSE futures slipped 0.3%.

The next health check on the AI industry will come as Anthropic prepares to price its shares later on Wednesday ahead of its market debut, which could value the company at as much as $1.4 trillion. The company has guided its IPO price to the top of its range or above, Bloomberg News reported.
